timecoded_text_to_speech.text: Hello, my name is Mary Wins Stanley O'Connor. It is my distinct honor and pleasure to seek
another term as a member of the Eilington Board of Assessors to represent you, my fellow
residents. I am a proud graduate of Arlington High School and have been an attorney for
40 years. In addition to my law degree, I have a master's degree in tax law from Boston
University Law School. My education, professional expertise, and training enable me to contribute
value to the Board of Assessors. We are fortunate to have an elected board which is well-balanced
and highly skilled. The elected board includes myself as an attorney, Gordon Jameson, who
is a community activist and activist and business person, and Williams Agata, an experienced
and licensed appraiser. The Board of Assessors is required by Massachusetts Law to assess
all personal property and real estate at full and fair cash value. There are approximately
14,500 properties in the town the Board must assess. In the context of doing so, the Board
must be transparent and accessible to residents so that they can understand the basis for their
property valuation and be informed of relief they may be entitled to, such as tax abatements,
exemptions, for seniors, the blind, veterans, among others. Other really, such as the deferral
of property taxes for seniors struggling to pay their real estate taxes, is also available.
The Board of Assessors effectively serves both the town of Arlington in the form of assessing
all property and the taxpayers who may apply for abatements or exemptions and who need to
be satisfied that their properties are being fairly assessed. If you have any questions,
please contact the Board of Assessors or please feel free to contact me directly at my office,
617-523-1010, or via email at moconner at koilaw.com. Again, thank you for permitting
me to continue to serve the town that educated me and provides a wonderful community in which
to live and raise my family.
